doc.title: Jack Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997

title: Going to Syracuse and getting homesick
summary: A Syracuse band hired him; alone in a room for the first time he hitchhiked home and cried, and describes his close family.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah, sure. Because then when the law was passed it was wide open, it was great. So this band from Syracuse was working in Sylvan Beach also, so they come over and they heard me because I played like colored people, you know, I played black style you know what I mean? And so they asked me to come to Syracuse. So I said, “Well you’ve got to ask my mother.” Well I couldn’t leave home, you know? So I introduced them, they came to my house, and they said they wanted me in Syracuse so my mother let me go. And they got me a room in Syracuse, and after everything was all over, we were playing, we stopped somewhere and had coffee, you know like that style, and then they drove me to the room where I had the room, now all of a sudden I’m all alone, you know what I mean? Everybody’s going to their homes and everything but I’m in a room, first time I’m away from my family, and boy I went to bed, but in about an hour I got up and I was hitchhiking back to Rome.
I didn’t know what, like to be outside of my house? That was very, ummm. So that I remember very vividly.
That’s very interesting. © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

My mother said, “What are you doing home?” Not what are you doing, like what happened? Here it is like three or four o’clock in the morning. She says, “You sick?” I said no, no, I’m all right, I just was homesick I told her, and I started crying, believe me.
Well you much have had a good home experience to make you want to come back.
Oh, yeah, oh gee, yeah. I was the oldest in the family and it was myself and then three sisters then another brother, then another sister. We were a very close family. A lot of love in the family.
Well after that first experience away from home —
You must have gotten over that.
Because you went on to play with some great people.
